children: Updated at 12:50 PM ET to include a response from Invitation Homes; updates stock movement.
Land & Buildings, the hedge fund led by real estate investor Jonathan Litt,
to Invitation Homes
shareholders on Monday urging the single-family home rental REIT to return at least $2B of capital annually to shareholders.
Invitation Homes
stock rose 1.1% in early afternoon trading on Monday.

The investor pointed out the gap between the value of the homes in its inventory and the value that its stock price reflects. Land & Buildings estimates an average value of $425K for each house Invitation owns, while its stock price implies a value of $270K per house. The estimated value supports a net asset value of ~$45 per share, including a frictional cost of 6% to sell each home, or ~65% higher than Invitation's current stock price.

"INVH has a unique ability to sell its assets one at a time to individual homebuyers, at retail prices and at scale, and to use the proceeds to return capital to shareholders either through repurchasing deeply discounted stock or distributing special dividends to shareholders," Litt said in the letter to shareholders.
Land & Buildings wants the REIT to commit to returning at least $2B of capital to shareholders annually on a leverage-neutral basis by repurchasing Invitation's
shares or distributing dividends. Those would be funded by selling homes, individually, for as long as the shares trade at a discount to NAV.

"We estimate this return of capital program could drive substantial annual accretion to both earnings and NAV per share, and with nearly $40B of gross asset value, we believe the company can sustain it for many years if necessary," the letter said.

Furthermore, the investor suggested that the company offer existing renters a path to ownership by offering a 6% rebate to cover the down payment. It's also asking the company to significantly cut back on its growth activities, including acquisitions and development.
Updated at 12:50 PM ET:
In an emailed statement to Seeking Alpha, Invitation Homes
responded to the letter, saying its board and management are committed to "acting in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders to deliver long-term, sustainable value."

Furthermore, the company said it's always open to hearing and considering perspectives from its shareholders. "Members of our board and management team have had numerous discussions with Land & Buildings over the past several months to better understand its views, as we would with any shareholder," a company spokesperson said. "While we are disappointed that Land & Buildings has chosen to make its issues public at this time, we remain open to further engagement."
In Invitation's

CFO Jonathan Olsen said, "This past year, we've repurchased nearly $1B of our stock, which represents 6% of our shares outstanding, funded in large part by proceeds from home sales." The company also announced a
program along with its Q3 results.

title: Activist urges Invitation Homes to return at least $2B to shareholders (updated)
